-   **Rarity note:** Migratory bird found throughout Florida in coastal shrubs, mangroves, pine flatwoods, hammocks and other areas of large cover.

## Natural history notes

A small migratory songbird characterized by gray-brown upperparts, streaked sides, a yellow rump, and yellow patches on the sides, with brighter breeding-plumage birds showing a white throat and more contrasting facial pattern. In Florida, it is a common winter visitor found in coastal scrub, mangroves, pine flatwoods, hammocks, forest edges, parks, yards, marsh edges, and other wooded or shrubby habitats. It feeds on insects, spiders, berries, and waxy fruits, often foraging in shrubs, trees, or on the ground and frequently forming mixed flocks during the nonbreeding season.
